text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. is not satisfied with Prime Minister Netanyahu's proposal and demands from him concrete calming steps.
- Order to soldiers: shoot at any Palestinian that nears your position in West Bank.
- Danny Nahmani asks court to prevent his estranged wife from using surrogate mother in Israel.
- Palestinian President Arafat heard tunnel would be opened at about the same time that the Israeli army chief of staff did.
- Israel archives permits publication of 1956 Sinai agreement between Israel, Britain, France; Israel has only copy of agreement which France lost and Britain's Anthony Eden burned.
- Treasury: incidents in the territories have not influenced the defence budget but have hurt growth.
- American pressure on Netanyahu begins as soon as he lands in Washington.
- Son of Jewish mayor of Jerusalem signs petition against army service in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
- Tender for Africa Israel to be offered today.
- Defence Minister Mordechai says a formula for dialogue with the Palestinians will be found.
- Egyptian President Mubarak: I am not optimistic about summit; I feel sorry for President Clinton.

- Poll: 60 percent say tunnel should stay open; 54 percent say opening was a mistake; 66 percent said weapons should not have been given to Palestinians; 80 percent support continued implementation of Oslo peace accords with PLO.
- U.S. family proposes acquiring 100 percent of Bank Mercantile.
